projects.title: Euterpe (Spotify Web App)
projects.summary: Named after the Greek Muse of music, Euterpe is a Spotify-integrated web app for tracking and visualizing listening habits. It was originally designed as a multi-user platform, but after Spotify's 2025 API policy changes restricted multi-user apps to organizations, the project pivoted into a personal analytics dashboard that publicly showcases only my listening data.
projects.description:
Euterpe is a full-stack music analytics platform that connects to the Spotify API through a Python Flask backend using the Spotipy client. It implements OAuth 2.0 authentication, token refresh, and session management, exposing pre-hydrated JSON endpoints consumed by a single-page vanilla JavaScript frontend.

The data layer enriches Spotify responses in memory, ranking albums by track frequency, identifying lesser-known tracks using popularity scores, and computing seasonal and release-year trends. Users can switch between time ranges such as four weeks, six months, or one year to analyze how listening preferences evolve over time.

The frontend mirrors Spotify's design language with responsive layouts, animated transitions, and asynchronous data fetching using Promise.all. It presents detailed breakdowns of top artists, albums, and playlists, along with analytical views such as long-term favorites and declining trends.

Euterpe was designed with technical scalability and efficiency in mind, emphasizing lightweight REST endpoints and a stateless architecture. Deployment supports Gunicorn-based production hosting and optional Docker usage.

The application prioritizes privacy by using read-only OAuth scopes and clearing session data on logout. No user data is permanently stored.
